section_summary: This section documents Japanese and American efforts to suppress narcotics trafficking, including new anti-smuggling controls aboard Nippon Yusen Kaisha ships, investigations of suspected traffickers, arrests in Japan and China, and reports of drug seizures. It also contains League of Nations material on international information-sharing and Japanese narcotics regulations. The final portion concerns a State–Treasury dispute over whether American Treasury representatives in Japan could work directly with local police or had to route requests through the American Embassy and Japanese Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2071: Measures by N.Y.K. Line Against Narcotics Smuggling
subfiles.from: E. R. Dickover, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese material describing anti-smuggling measures adopted aboard Nippon Yusen Kaisha ships serving American ports.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2071: the Foreign Office describes N.Y.K. measures against narcotics smuggling by Japanese seamen, especially on San Francisco and Seattle services.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office Note on N.Y.K. Preventive Measures
subfiles.from: Kuriyama, Director of the Treaty Bureau
subfiles.about: Reports that Nippon Yusen Kaisha has adopted narcotics-smuggling precautions on its San Francisco and Seattle routes.
subfiles.summary: Kuriyama says the Metropolitan Police reported more smuggling by crews at Pacific Coast ports and lists the company's preventive measures.

subfiles.title: Nippon Yusen Kaisha Measures to Prevent Narcotics Smuggling
subfiles.from: Marine Transportation Section, Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Lists shipboard surveillance and access controls introduced on seven trans-Pacific vessels.
subfiles.summary: The company assigns special searching officers and assistants to vessels on its Hong Kong–San Francisco and Kobe–Seattle services. It also restricts crew landings and visitors, changes identification cards for ship peddlers, installs correspondence boxes, and increases rewards for finding narcotics.

subfiles.title: Confidential Transmittal of Despatch No. 2071
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo Embassy despatch on N.Y.K. anti-smuggling measures for confidential Treasury use.
subfiles.summary: State confidentially sends Treasury Despatch No. 2071 on safeguards aboard vessels serving San Francisco and Seattle.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese Narcotics Officials
subfiles.about: Cross-references a telegram identifying K. Kameyama as Japan’s chief narcotics-enforcement official.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Kuriyama wished to consult Kameyama on the feasibility of Thompson's plan.

subfiles.title: Customs Memorandum on Schwartz and Lessing Investigation
subfiles.about: Forwards the results of the San Francisco investigation of Max Schwartz and Ben Lessing.
subfiles.summary: Customs encloses a San Francisco report on the arrival and surveillance of Schwartz and Lessing, who sailed from Yokohama on the Taiyo Maru.

subfiles.title: Report on the Arrival and Surveillance of Schwartz and Lessing
subfiles.from: Frederick S. Freed, Supervising Customs Agent, San Francisco
subfiles.about: Reports surveillance and background investigation of Schwartz and Lessing after their arrival from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Schwartz and Lessing arrived October 12 and were watched; the original allegation came from J. O. Brown, and no narcotics link was found, though Los Angeles was asked to continue surveillance.

subfiles.title: Letter from Mary and Jim Harris to Grace and J. O.
subfiles.about: Announces the Harrises’ planned return from Japan by way of Seattle and San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Letter from Mary and Jim Harris arriving at Seattle on the Heian Maru July 5; J. O. Brown asks Customs to keep it confidential.

subfiles.title: J. O. Brown’s Information on Lessing and Schwartz
subfiles.about: Supplies allegations concerning Lessing, Schwartz, their photography operation, and possible mail fraud.
subfiles.summary: Brown describes Lessing and recounts reports that Schwartz destroyed business records, failed to deliver paid photographs, and exploited associates. He suggests possible sources of further information while warning that the Harrises and their wives fear retaliation.

subfiles.title: J. O. Brown’s Identification of the Schwartz Family
subfiles.to: John V. Lewis, Collector of Internal Revenue
subfiles.about: Forwards photographs identifying William Schwartz, his wife, and their children.
subfiles.summary: Brown identifies Schwartz as former head of International Movie Flash and says Seattle and Shanghai Customs were investigating him.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Yokohama on the Schwartz–Lessing Investigation
subfiles.about: Transmits the Treasury report on the San Francisco investigation of Schwartz and Lessing.
subfiles.summary: Instruction sends Yokohama Customs' findings on suspected traffickers Schwartz and Lessing.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan Advertiser Article to the Public Health Service
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury, for the Public Health Service
subfiles.about: Sends a photostatic copy of an article on the first year of Tokyo’s anti-drug clinic.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a Japan Advertiser article on free treatment facilities and expansion plans to the Public Health Service; Customs gets copies.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan Advertiser Article to Customs
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury, for the Customs Agency Service
subfiles.about: Sends duplicate photostats of the article on Tokyo’s anti-drug clinic.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Japan Advertiser article to Customs, with a copy to the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Successful First Year for Anti-Drug Clinic Brings Plans to Extend Free Cure Facilities
subfiles.about: Reports patient numbers, treatment results, and expansion plans at a Tokyo narcotics sanatorium.
subfiles.summary: Anti-drug clinic treated 757 patients in its first year with 120 relapses; plans expansion as demand exceeds capacity.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the Nagai–Yamada Letter
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report about a Japanese letter found on Toshiyoshi Nagai that mentioned Tatsuo Yamada.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Yamada, an employee aboard the Koyei Maru; Treasury asked that the information reach Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Translation of Report on a Tokyo Narcotics Ring
subfiles.about: Describes arrests of Japanese medical practitioners and Korean suspects for cocaine, heroin, and morphine offenses.
subfiles.summary: A Minami-Senju policeman’s discovery of a morphine user led investigators through several suppliers to Tei Yutoku, whose house contained cocaine and heroin. Confessions implicated additional suspects, including Kyo Kenki, Kinzo Iide, and Yujiro Iwata, and the case was sent to prosecutors. The Japanese-language original follows the English translation.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Edwin and Josie Russell
subfiles.about: Reports the Russells’ impending voyage to North America and Edwin Russell’s associations with suspected traffickers.
subfiles.summary: Telegram: Edwin and Josie Russell, sailing on the Empress of Japan, were friendly with Lewis and Soriano and might know of Yokohama narcotics activity.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference Identifying the Treasury Attaché at Kobe
subfiles.about: Identifies Martin G. Scott as the Treasury Attaché at Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The brief note supplies Scott’s name and post. It directs readers to another decimal-file location concerning narcotics information.

subfiles.title: Confidential Transmittal of the Russell Telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Yokohama telegram concerning Edwin and Josie Russell’s expected arrival.
subfiles.summary: State highlights Russell's friendships with Lewis and Soriano, Schwartz associates; copies go confidentially to Customs.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan Chronicle Article on Osaka Drug Smugglers
subfiles.about: Sends an article concerning arrests by Osaka police for illicit narcotics trafficking.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the December 2 Japan Chronicle clipping on a group accused of exporting narcotics through Formosa to South China.

subfiles.title: Drug Smugglers: Gang of Fourteen Arrested by Osaka Police
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of fourteen people accused of exporting narcotics through Takao to South China.
subfiles.summary: Osumi and thirteen associates allegedly bought drugs for shipment to Hoshino in Formosa; police estimated turnover at ¥285,000 from 1934 to 1936.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of ‘Has the Dope Trade Begun to Backfire on Japan?’
subfiles.about: Forwards a photostatic copy of a China Weekly Review article on Japan and the narcotics trade.
subfiles.summary: Sends Treasury the clipping 'Has the Dope Trade Begun to Backfire on Japan?' on Japanese territories and shipments to the Pacific coast.

subfiles.title: Has the Dope Trade Begun to ‘Backfire’ on Japan?
subfiles.about: Criticizes narcotics conditions in Japanese-controlled territories and reports allegations by Toshiyoshi Nagai.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt contrasts proposed controls in the Kwantung Leased Territory with opium monopolies in Formosa and Manchukuo. It reports that Nagai claimed an illicit factory near Nagasaki supplied a ring using trans-Pacific sailors to carry drugs to American ports. The same clipping text appears on both pages.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Anglo-Japanese Narcotics Information Agreement
subfiles.about: Sends a League of Nations document reproducing the British–Japanese agreement on narcotics intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Anglo-Japanese agreement by notes of March 30, 1936 on reciprocal cooperation in collecting and sending information on illicit drug trafficking.

subfiles.title: League Document on the British–Japanese Narcotics Agreement
subfiles.about: Publishes the exchanged British and Japanese notes establishing reciprocal narcotics-intelligence cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Robert H. Clive and Kōki Hirota record arrangements for diplomatic, consular, police, and customs authorities to exchange information about known drug traffickers. The agreement extends to British colonies, protectorates, mandated territories, Australia, New Zealand, and India. Four schedules identify the competent authorities throughout Japan’s territories and the British Empire.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo Transmitting the Anglo-Japanese Agreement
subfiles.about: Provides the Tokyo Embassy with the League document on British–Japanese narcotics cooperation.
subfiles.summary: The instruction summarizes the notes exchanged on March 30, 1936. It encloses the agreement for the Embassy’s information.

subfiles.title: List of League Narcotics Documents Forwarded from Geneva
subfiles.about: Lists League of Nations annual reports and regulations on narcotics sent to Washington.
subfiles.summary: List of League narcotics documents from Geneva: 1935 reports for Japan and others, and Japanese narcotics laws in Korea, Taiwan and Kwantung.

subfiles.title: League Communiqué on Japanese Territorial Narcotics Laws
subfiles.about: Distributes laws and regulations promulgated in Korea, Taiwan, and the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: League communiqué: Japanese territorial narcotics laws form part of Japan's 1935 report, circulated under Article 21 of the 1931 Convention.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the Buitenzorg Seizure
subfiles.about: Cross-references a confidential League report on heroin and morphine seized at Buitenzorg, Java.
subfiles.summary: The seizure occurred on October 27, 1936. The note directs readers to another decimal-file location containing the report.

subfiles.title: Confidential Instruction on the Buitenzorg Narcotics Case
subfiles.about: Transmits a confidential Netherlands report on a heroin and morphine seizure in Java.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is instructed not to disclose the report to Japanese authorities. The Department notes that M. Yuki had previously been implicated in smuggling into Canada and the United States and adds information about Formosan Chinese travelers suspected of carrying heroin aboard the Hozan Maru.

subfiles.title: Geneva Telegram on Japanese Arrests and Far Eastern Narcotics Conditions
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, for Harold N. Graves
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese arrests linked to the Heian Maru case and strong international criticism of narcotics conditions under Japanese control.
subfiles.summary: Geneva: Japanese police arrested suspects at Dalian and Kobe after inquiries about a Seattle seizure; US, Egyptian and Canadian representatives exposed Far Eastern narcotics links to the US.

subfiles.title: Customs Report on Edwin and Josie Russell’s Entry
subfiles.about: Reports that the Russells entered at Blaine without suspicious conduct or baggage.
subfiles.summary: Customs found nothing suspicious when Edwin and Josie Russell entered December 30; they visited relatives near Portland, Oregon.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan’s 1935 Annual Narcotics Report to Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends Japan’s League of Nations annual report on opium and dangerous drugs for 1935.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Japan's 1935 annual narcotics report, with sections on Taiwan, Kwantung and Chinese concessions, to Treasury and other agencies.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo Transmitting Japan’s 1935 Narcotics Report
subfiles.about: Provides the Embassy with Japan’s 1935 annual report on opium and dangerous drugs.
subfiles.summary: Instruction to Tokyo transmitting Japan's 1935 narcotics report under Article 21 of the 1931 Convention.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese Territorial Narcotics Regulations
subfiles.about: Forwards League and Japanese texts of narcotics laws for Korea, Taiwan, and the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends four copies of the League communiqué and of two Taiwan Government-General ordinances from August 1935. Because only one original Japanese annual report was received, it remains in State’s files, while photostats of previously untransmitted Kwantung regulations are supplied to Treasury.

subfiles.title: Instruction Reporting the Russells’ Border Examination
subfiles.about: Informs the Consulate of the examination given Edwin and Josie Russell at Blaine, Washington.
subfiles.summary: Instruction encloses a March 9 Treasury report on the Russells' border examination, recalling their friendship with Lewis and Soriano.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Article on Fifty Narcotics Suspects
subfiles.about: Sends duplicate copies of a Japan Advertiser clipping about mass arrests in Osaka and Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The clipping concerns more than fifty suspected narcotics sellers. It is forwarded for the information of the Customs Agency Service.

subfiles.title: Police Hold 50 Suspects as Sellers of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Reports arrests tied to more than ¥200,000 in narcotics sales across Kyushu, Kansai, and Kantō.
subfiles.summary: Police detained Hanazono Bando, whose confession expanded the probe; Bando, Naito and Isono were regional operators supplied by two Osaka pharmacies.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on James S. Dolan
subfiles.about: Cross-references a despatch concerning James S. Dolan’s passport application and suspected narcotics involvement.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 92: James Dolan's activities appeared centered in Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Geneva Telegram on Japanese Narcotics Arrests
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, for Harold N. Graves
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report of arrests connected with the Heian Maru seizure and international criticism of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Geneva telegram: arrests at Dalian and Kobe after the Seattle case, with US, Egyptian and Canadian representatives pressing Japan.

subfiles.title: League Report on Prepared Opium Seized from the Serooskerke
subfiles.from: Japanese Government via the League of Nations
subfiles.about: Reports the seizure of prepared opium from Chinese stokers aboard a Dutch ship at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: League report: sixteen stokers arrested June 25, 1936 smoking opium aboard the Serooskerke; fourteen released, charges against two dismissed.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of League Seizure Reports to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards League of Nations documents concerning seizures of opium and other dangerous drugs.
subfiles.summary: Transmits League seizure reports, including confidential document O.C.S./Confidential/260 of May 22, 1937, to Customs.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Russell Pasha’s Statements
subfiles.about: Records a request for information about statements attributed to Russell Pasha concerning heroin exports from Japanese concessions in China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Treasury asks a telegram to Fuller at Geneva seeking clarification of Russell Pasha of Egypt's Central Narcotics Bureau.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese Narcotics Suppression in China
subfiles.about: Cross-references a telegram reporting Japanese efforts to curb narcotics trafficking in China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 159 from Johnson on Japanese narcotics suppression in China.

subfiles.title: Peiping Telegram on Japanese Narcotics Enforcement
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese statements about prosecutions, deportations, and difficulties suppressing narcotics trafficking in Beijing.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese consular police chief claimed that about 200 Japanese subjects had been prosecuted and about 100 deported during the preceding year. An Embassy official said suppression was complicated by the need to find alternative employment for traffickers. Johnson believed disagreement among Japanese officials was preventing rapid and effective action.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Treasury Access to Japanese Police Information
subfiles.from: G. A. Morlock, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Records John W. Bulkley’s complaint that new Embassy instructions restricted Treasury representatives’ access to local Japanese police.
subfiles.summary: Morlock explains Japan requires narcotics-information requests to pass via the Embassy and Foreign Office; direct cooperation efforts failed, and Bulkley asked that no action be taken pending a Graves-Hornbeck discussion.

subfiles.title: Graves Letter Requesting Restoration of Earlier Arrangements
subfiles.about: Requests State Department action allowing Treasury representatives in Japan to resume obtaining information through local police.
subfiles.summary: Graves asks Hornbeck to consider restoring arrangements preceding the Embassy's new instruction, enclosing Customs and Scott correspondence.

subfiles.title: Gorman Memorandum on the State–Treasury Cooperation Agreement
subfiles.about: Argues that the Embassy’s restriction on local police contacts conflicts with the State–Treasury cooperation agreement.
subfiles.summary: Gorman quotes the March 25 agreement requiring diplomatic and consular officers to assist Treasury representatives in overseas drug-smuggling investigations. He contends that the Kobe Consulate’s new practice appears inconsistent with that agreement and suggests raising the matter with State officials.

subfiles.title: Scott Report on Narcotics Investigations in Japan
subfiles.from: Martin G. Scott, Treasury Attaché, Kobe
subfiles.about: Explains how Embassy centralization would impair timely tracking of suspected narcotics traffickers in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Scott says routing every request through Tokyo causes delays, citing the Wirthmuller case, and asks whether to rely on private sources or approach local police.

subfiles.title: Consul Winthrop Scott’s Letter Implementing Embassy Instructions
subfiles.from: Winthrop R. Scott, American Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Notifies the Treasury Attaché that future requests about suspected traffickers must be referred to the Tokyo Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The Consul quotes the Embassy’s April 19 instruction centralizing exchanges through the American and Japanese governments. He states that the Consulate will comply while continuing to cooperate within its standing instructions.

subfiles.title: Morlock Memorandum to Hornbeck on Graves’s Complaint
subfiles.about: Recommends discussing Graves’s complaint and requesting the Tokyo Embassy’s explanation of its April 19 instruction.
subfiles.summary: Morlock notes the State-Treasury agreement had not reached Tokyo when the Embassy issued its restrictive instruction, and recommends a telegram seeking the Embassy's comments.

subfiles.title: Graves Letter Forwarding Scott’s May 11 Report
subfiles.about: Provides copies of Martin G. Scott’s latest report on narcotics investigations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Graves sends the Commissioner of Customs three copies of Scott's May 11 letter after speaking with Hornbeck.

subfiles.title: Scott Report on Hyōgo Police Offer of Direct Cooperation
subfiles.from: Martin G. Scott, Treasury Attaché, Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports that Hyōgo police requested immediate direct notification of suspected traffickers to avoid bureaucratic delays.
subfiles.summary: Hyogo detectives offer direct telephone or personal contact before formal reporting after the Tensaka case and Nonaka's escape; Scott recommends trying it and requests a small confidential fund.

subfiles.title: State Department Reply to Graves
subfiles.about: States that Treasury had misunderstood State Department action and promises to seek the Tokyo Embassy’s comments.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck acknowledges Graves’s May 28 letter and its enclosed Customs and Kobe correspondence. He says State is telegraphing the Embassy with the issue and will communicate further after receiving a reply.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo Requesting Review of Narcotics Cooperation Procedures
subfiles.about: Asks the Embassy and Kobe Consul to reconsider procedures governing cooperation with Treasury narcotics investigators.
subfiles.summary: Department tells the Kobe Consul to discuss Scott's reports sympathetically and the Embassy to telegraph comments on restoring earlier narcotics cooperation arrangements.
